extracted.intended_audience: design patent applicants, patent practitioners, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the required elements, form, and content of a U.S. design patent application filed under 35 U.S.C. chapter 16, including specification, claim, drawings/photographs, titles, and permissible/impermissible statements. Intended to direct preparation and examination of design patent filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement of application elements (37 CFR 1.154)
rubrics_metrics.description: The elements of the design application, if applicable, should appear in the following order: (1) Design application transmittal form; (2) Fee transmittal form; (3) Application data sheet (§ 1.76); (4) Specification; (5) Drawings or photographs; (6) The inventor's oath or declaration (§ 1.153(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The specification should include sections in order: (1) Preamble (name of applicant, title of design, brief description of nature and intended use); (2) Cross-reference to related applications (unless in ADS); (3) Statement regarding federally sponsored research or development; (4) Description of the figure(s) of the drawing; (5) Feature description; (6) A single claim. Section headings should be uppercase without underlining or bold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title must designate particular article (37 CFR 1.153)
rubrics_metrics.description: The title of the design must designate the particular article in which the design is embodied; no description other than reference to the drawing is ordinarily required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The title identifies the article and may contribute to defining the scope of the claim. The title may be directed to the entire article or only a portion but may not be directed to less than the claimed design shown in full lines. A descriptive, accurate title aids classification and public notice. Amendments to title must have antecedent basis and not introduce new matter. Title and claim must correspond; examiners should object to inconsistencies under 37 CFR 1.153.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preamble content
rubrics_metrics.description: Preamble should state the name of the applicant, title of the design, and a brief description of the nature and intended use of the article in which the design is embodied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If title is broad, incorporate description of nature/intended use into the preamble. For articles with multiple functions or independent parts, title must define them as a single entity (e.g., combined, set, pair, unit assembly).

rubrics_metrics.name: Title/claim correspondence and examiner latitude
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the claim defines the subject matter, examiners should afford substantial latitude in title/claim language but require amendment if language is clearly misdescriptive, inaccurate, or unclear (would result in a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of vague terms like 'or the like' directed to the environment is allowed for environment wording in many cases, but indefiniteness can arise when such language refers to the area of articles defining the subject matter. Amendments to the title must be made throughout the application (except oath/declaration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification description requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: No description of the design beyond a brief description of the drawing is generally necessary since the drawings are ordinarily the best description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Descriptions of the figures need not follow a particular format, but unclear/inaccurate descriptions should be objected to. A description may be included at applicant's option or provided in a separate paper; any descriptive matter added after filing that constitutes new matter is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible specification statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Permissible statements include: (1) description of appearance of portions not illustrated; (2) description disclaiming portions not shown as forming no part of claimed design; (3) statement indicating purpose of broken lines (environmental structure/boundaries); (4) statement denoting nature and intended use; (5) 'characteristic features' statement describing a feature of novelty or nonobviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissible statements must be present in the original filing if they later serve as antecedent basis. A 'characteristic features' statement may be included but may not serve as the basis for determining patentability—the overall appearance controls. Examiners will not suggest the inclusion of a characteristic feature statement; it is at applicant’s option.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impermissible specification statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Not permissible: (1) disclaimer statements directed to any portion of the claimed design shown in solid lines in the drawings (not permitted in specification of an issued design patent, though may be included in original application for antecedent basis); (2) statements describing or suggesting other embodiments not illustrated (except mirror images or shapes evident from shown view); (3) statements describing matters directed to function or unrelated to design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such statements, if included improperly, should be canceled; they may constitute new matter or improperly broaden scope. See MPEP § 2909.02 for international application disclaimers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patents concern ornamental appearance only
rubrics_metrics.description: Design patent applications are concerned solely with the ornamental appearance of an article of manufacture; functional and/or structural features are of no concern in design cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Function and structure are handled in utility patents. Avoid functional language in design specifications and claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristic feature statement caution
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'characteristic features' statement describing a particular feature of novelty or nonobviousness may be permissible but the patentability of the claimed design is based on the overall appearance, not the specified feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such statements may later limit the claim. If used, phrase as 'The characteristic feature of the design resides in [feature].' Insert brief but accurate description if included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single claim requirement (37 CFR 1.153)
rubrics_metrics.description: A design patent application may only include a single claim. The claim shall be in formal terms to the ornamental design for the article (specifying name) as shown, or as shown and described. More than one claim is neither required nor permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The standard claim wording is 'The ornamental design for [article] as shown.' If the specification includes descriptive matter or modified forms, add 'and described' after 'shown.' The article description in the claim should be consistent with the title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full lines vs. broken lines in drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Full (solid) lines in the drawing show the claimed design; broken lines may be used for some purposes (e.g., environmental structure) but are not permitted to indicate unimportant or immaterial portions of the claimed design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broken lines may not be used to show hidden planes/surfaces or alternate positions of design components with full and broken lines in same view. Use broken lines to indicate environment or boundaries that form no part of design and explain their purpose in the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency and clarity of drawings/photographs (37 CFR 1.152)
rubrics_metrics.description: The design must be represented by a drawing that complies with § 1.84 and must contain a sufficient number of views to constitute a complete disclosure of the appearance of the design. Drawings/photographs must be clear and complete so that nothing of the design is left to conjecture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate surface shading to show character/contour (solid black shading only to represent the color black). Photographs submitted in lieu of drawings must be limited to the design claimed and must not show environmental structure. If inconsistencies among views render overall appearance unclear, the claim should be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(a)/(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Views required and when a single planar view suffices
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings should contain a sufficient number of views (front, rear, top, bottom, sides) to disclose the complete appearance. Where three-dimensional aspects are not claimed, a single plan- or planar-view may be sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perspective views are suggested for 3D designs. If a perspective view clearly discloses surfaces, other views may not be required. Duplicate or flat views without ornamentation may be omitted if the specification explains omission (e.g., 'other side identical' or 'bottom flat and devoid of surface ornamentation').

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement drawing sheets and labeling (37 CFR 1.121(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrected replacement drawing sheets in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121(d) are required in reply to an Office action to avoid abandonment; replacement sheets must include all figures appearing on the immediate prior version of the sheet even if only one figure is amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacement sheets must be labeled in the top margin as 'Replacement Sheet' or 'New Sheet'. If a drawing figure is canceled, remove it from the replacement sheet and renumber remaining figures; provide annotations or an 'Annotated Sheet' showing canceled figures in the amendment or remarks section. If changes not accepted, applicant informed in next Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid introducing new matter in drawings (35 U.S.C. 132; 37 CFR 1.121(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: When preparing new or replacement drawings, be careful to avoid introducing new matter; new matter is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs may be used to notify applicant of necessity for good drawings. Amendments that reveal underlying configurations not apparent in original filing may be treated as new matter (e.g., removal of three-dimensional surface treatment that reveals underlying configuration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity for good drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: The drawing constitutes the whole disclosure of the design and must be so well executed in clarity and completeness that nothing regarding the design is left to conjecture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An insufficient drawing may be fatal to validity (35 U.S.C. 112(a)) and may negatively affect the effective filing date in a continuing application. Use proper shading and number of views; ensure consistency across views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surface treatment disclosure rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Surface treatment (shape/configuration plus any indicia, contrasting color/materials, graphic representations, or other ornamentation) must be applied to or embodied in an article of manufacture; surface treatment per se is not proper subject matter for a design patent under 35 U.S.C. 171.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surface treatment must be shown in full lines if claimed or in broken lines if unclaimed. Disclosure of surface treatment in drawing/photograph is prima facie evidence applicant considered it integral to the claimed design. Applicant may remove surface treatment only if underlying configuration without surface treatment was apparent in original application; removing three-dimensional surface treatment that is integral will introduce new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographs and color drawings rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs are not ordinarily permitted but may be accepted if they are the only practicable medium; color drawings/photographs are permitted if filed according to 37 CFR 1.84(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If color drawings/photographs submitted, include statement in specification: 'The file of this patent contains at least one drawing/photograph executed in color.' Electronic filing via USPTO may require only one set; non-electronic filings require three sets. Photographs must be of sufficient quality to show all details or objections will be raised and patent not issued until acceptable photographs are submitted. Photographs and ink drawings must not be combined in the same application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color and lining-for-color guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Where drawings are lined for color, include the statement 'The drawing is lined for color.' Lining entire surfaces for color may interfere with clear showing of design because shading cannot be used simultaneously to define contours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If color drawings/photographs filed, color is considered integral to disclosure and claim; omission of color later is permitted only if it is clear applicant had possession of underlying configuration without color at filing. Some designs disclosed in color cannot be accurately depicted in black-and-white lined drawings (e.g., multiple shades).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and description of broken lines (environment and boundaries)
rubrics_metrics.description: Broken lines may illustrate environmental structure if clearly designated as environment in the specification; a descriptive statement explaining broken lines should be inserted (e.g., 'The broken line showing of [structure] is for the purpose of illustrating [portions of the article/environmental structure] and forms no part of the claimed design.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where superimposed broken lines showing environmental structure obscure full-line claimed disclosure, include a separate figure showing broken lines in addition to figures showing only claimed subject matter. When broken lines define a boundary of the design, use the statement: 'The [type] broken line(s) define the bounds of the claimed design and form no part thereof.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using broken lines to indicate immaterial features
rubrics_metrics.description: Broken lines used for the purpose of indicating unimportant or immaterial features of the design are not permitted; there are no portions of a claimed design which are immaterial or unimportant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broken lines may not be used to exclude parts of solid-line claimed features; consult In re Blum and In re Zahn for precedent. If environmental broken lines obscure claimed full-line disclosure, require separate figure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency among views and consequences of inconsistency
rubrics_metrics.description: When inconsistencies are found among the views, the examiner should object and request that the views be made consistent; if inconsistencies are so significant that overall appearance is unclear, reject the claim under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) and (b) as nonenabling and indefinite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrected drawing sheets must be submitted to resolve inconsistencies. In appeals, drawings must be corrected prior to appeal if required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on combining photographs and ink drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs and ink drawings are not permitted to be combined as formal drawings in one application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If photographs are used in lieu of ink drawings, they must be limited to the design claimed and not disclose environmental structure. Combining the two leads to high probability of inconsistencies between elements.
